items.title: Eddie Dawson Interview, 1972-04-05
items.q: He'd make up a rhyme on him... You'd go around your pocket, give him a couple of dollars a piece.

ctx.x: He did. He played. Man, he's tuned it up until he's getting high, you know. He'd, as long as it could make a bump. Boom, boom, boom. He'd be slapping, you know. He could rhyme, though. He made his money off of singing and rhyming. Yeah. I see, like he knew your name Clyde. Clyde, somebody tell you. Kind of, he found out he could, he could rhyme up a song on you, and you wouldn't, you think you was one and you'd be one and how he knew you, you see. He'd make up a rhyme on him. Doesn't know it's quite natural.…
Did you ever hit, you played guitar with him then? Yeah.
